summary: On a Sabbath in Capernaum, Jesus teaches with authority in the synagogue and commands an unclean spirit to come out of a man, and His fame spreads.
key_insight: The people were amazed twice, first at His teaching and then at the exorcism, and both times the reason given is authority. The voice that taught them in the synagogue was the voice the unclean spirit had to obey.
story: Jesus and His new followers went into Capernaum, and on the Sabbath He entered the synagogue and taught. {Mk} The people were astonished at His teaching, for He taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes. {Mk}

In the synagogue that day was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out with a loud voice, {Lk} “Let us alone! What have we to do with You, Jesus of Nazareth? Did You come to destroy us? I know who You are,” and he named Him: “the Holy One of God!”

Jesus rebuked him: “Be quiet, and come out of him!” The unclean spirit convulsed the man and cried out with a loud voice. {Mk} It threw him down in the middle of them and came out of him without hurting him. {Lk}

Everyone was amazed. They asked one another, “What is this? What new doctrine is this? For with authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him.” {Mk} Immediately His fame spread throughout all the region around Galilee. {Mk}
differences: Mark says the people were astonished because He taught “as one having authority, and not as the scribes”; Luke says “His word was with authority.”
Luke alone says the demon threw the man down “in their midst” and came out without hurting him. Mark says the spirit convulsed him and cried out with a loud voice.
The crowd’s words differ: “What new doctrine is this?” in Mark, “What a word this is!” in Luke. Luke adds that Jesus commands with “authority and power.”

scene.label: The synagogue
scene.text: Visitors today see a white limestone synagogue built centuries after Jesus. Beneath it lie dark basalt foundations that many archaeologists think belong to the earlier synagogue where Jesus taught. Luke later notes that a Gentile centurion had built Capernaum’s synagogue (Luke 7:5).

scene.label: Not as the scribes
scene.text: The scribes were trained teachers of the Law. As later Jewish writings show, their custom was to support a teaching by citing earlier authorities. Jesus taught on His own authority, and everyone in the room could hear the difference.

scene.label: Exorcists
scene.text: Jewish exorcists of the time were known for spells and rituals. Josephus describes one who used a ring, a root and incantations said to come from Solomon, and Acts tells of exorcists who borrowed the name of Jesus (Acts 19:13). Jesus used a single command in His own name.

witnesses.mark: Makes this Jesus’ first miracle, right after the call of the four fishermen. Mark frames it with the word “authority” at the start and the end, and he loves the word “immediately.” From his first chapter, Mark shows Jesus invading the territory of evil.
witnesses.luke: Sets the scene right after Nazareth rejected Him: the hometown that would not receive Him is followed by a town amazed at His word. Luke notes that the man was not hurt, and he adds that Jesus commands “with authority and power.”

seeing.reveals: Jesus speaks with the authority of God Himself. He needs no ritual and no borrowed name. One word from Him silences a demon and sets a captive free.
seeing.living: The man was in the synagogue on the Sabbath, in the place of worship, and still in bondage. Being near religious things is not the same as being free. Bring what binds you into the light of Jesus’ word, and trust the One the demons themselves fear.
seeing.ponder: What in your life needs to hear Jesus say, “Be quiet, and come out”?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus’ word carries God’s authority: it teaches the mind and frees the captive.
preaching.watch_for: “Authority” frames the scene (1:22, 27). The demon asks, “Did You come to destroy us?” Mark’s answer comes in 3:27: Jesus has come to bind the strong man and plunder his house.
